The department chair wants to understand the workload distribution among Teaching Assistants across all courses to make informed staffing decisions for next semester. Pull TA enrollment data across all courses along with assignment and submission counts to assess the workload each TA is responsible for.

Create an Excel file called TA_Workload_Report.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Course Workload" and contain the following columns: Course_Name, Course_Code, TA_Count, Assignment_Count, Submission_Count, and Submissions_Per_TA. Submissions_Per_TA should be the Submission_Count divided by TA_Count, rounded to 1 decimal place. If a course has no TAs, set Submissions_Per_TA to 0. Sort the rows by Course_Name alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Summary" with rows for Total_Courses, Total_TAs (sum of all TA_Count across courses), Avg_TAs_Per_Course (rounded to 1 decimal), Max_Assignment_Count (the highest assignment count among all courses), and Most_Loaded_Course (the course name with the highest Submissions_Per_TA).

Then create a Notion page called "TA Staffing Overview" that summarizes the key findings from the workload analysis including total courses, total TAs, and which course has the heaviest TA workload.

Finally, email the report to dept_chair@university.edu with subject "TA Workload Report" and a brief summary in the body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one compact Explore agent per concrete course. Each course has a true local dependency from its assignment list to its bulk submission-count call, but courses are independent.

The main agent calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), validates unique returned IDs/codes/full names, and instantiates one literal prompt per course.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 22 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal course below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course Explore agent for course_id=1 (AAA-2013J): first call canvas_list_assignments(course_id=1, include_submissions=false), validate unique assignment IDs, and freeze that literal assignment_ids list. In the next response call natively in parallel: canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=1, page=1, per_page=1, type=["TaEnrollment"]) taking TA_Count from pagination.total_count without fetching TA rows; and canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=1, assignment_ids=<literal returned assignment IDs>, student_ids=["all"], grouped=false, page=1, per_page=1) taking Submission_Count from pagination.total_count without fetching later submission pages. Return only {course_id:1,course_code:"AAA-2013J",course_name,assignment_ids,assignment_count,ta_count,submission_count,assignment_response_count,ta_pagination,submission_pagination}. Do not modify Canvas.

Then dispatch the three independent output branches in one native-parallel response from the frozen canonical payload:

- coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole-write TA_Workload_Report.xlsx in the dynamically resolved workspace with exactly Course Workload and Summary — exact headers, all course rows, literal values and rounding — reading both populated ranges back.
- coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole-own the Notion page TA Staffing Overview: search and retrieve all exact-title candidates, stop without mutation on duplicates, create exactly once only if absent, and append the complete canonical paragraph exactly once only if absent. After the outputs, reconcile workbook, Notion and email against the canonical payload; do not dispatch an aggregation or verification agent.

nodes.text:
You are planning a multi-system data task. Produce an ordered subtask plan with dispatch decisions (self = main agent, explore = read-only exploration, coder = execution) and dependency/parallelism notes for each subtask.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the user):
The department chair wants to understand workload distribution among Teaching Assistants across all courses. We must:
1. Pull TA enrollment data across ALL courses in Canvas, along with assignment counts and submission counts per course, to assess TA workload.
2. Create an Excel file at <workspace>/TA_Workload_Report.xlsx with two sheets:
   - Sheet "Course Workload": columns Course_Name, Course_Code, TA_Count, Assignment_Count, Submission_Count, Submissions_Per_TA. Submissions_Per_TA = Submission_Count / TA_Count rounded to 1 decimal place; if TA_Count is 0, set Submissions_Per_TA to 0. Sort rows by Course_Name alphabetically.
   - Sheet "Summary": rows for Total_Courses, Total_TAs (sum of TA_Count), Avg_TAs_Per_Course (rounded to 1 decimal), Max_Assignment_Count (highest assignment count), Most_Loaded_Course (course name with highest Submissions_Per_TA).
3. Create a Notion page titled "TA Staffing Overview" summarizing key findings (total courses, total TAs, heaviest TA workload course).
4. Send an email to dept_chair@university.edu with subject "TA Workload Report" and a brief summary in the body.

AVAILABLE TOOLS (for your read-only planning investigation, if needed):
- Canvas MCP: list courses (canvas_list_courses), get course grades/enrollments (canvas_get_course_grades with type[] filter e.g. TaEnrollment), list course users (canvas_list_course_users), list assignments (canvas_list_assignments), list assignment submissions (canvas_list_assignment_submissions), list student submissions (canvas_list_student_submissions).
- Excel MCP: create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, etc.
- Notion MCP: API-post-search, API-post-page, etc.
- Email MCP: send_email, get_emails, etc.
- Filesystem MCP: read/write files under the workspace.

Your job: inspect the Canvas instance (read-only) to understand how TA enrollments, assignments, and submissions are structured (e.g., which enrollment role type represents TAs, e.g. TaEnrollment), and then produce a plan. Specifically verify:
- How to enumerate all courses (canvas_list_courses returns courses with id, name, course_code).
- How to get TA count per course (canvas_get_course_grades with type filter, or canvas_list_course_users and count role=TaEnrollment / TA role).
- How to get assignment count per course (canvas_list_assignments).
- How to get submission count per course (canvas_list_student_submissions or canvas_list_assignment_submissions aggregated).

Deliverable: An ordered list of subtasks, each with: dispatch decision (self/explore/coder), what to do, what data it consumes/produces, whether it can run in parallel with siblings, and a verification step. Also note any pitfalls (e.g., pagination, counting submissions per assignment vs per course, distinguishing TA role from teacher/student roles). Keep it concise but complete.

You are collecting workload metrics from a Canvas LMS instance using the Canvas MCP tools, then saving the results as JSON files in the workspace.

WORKSPACE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-ta-workload-excel-email/workspace/

CONTEXT: We need per-course metrics for ALL 22 courses below to build a TA workload report. For each course we need: TA_Count (number of TaEnrollment enrollments), Assignment_Count (number of assignments), Submission_Count (total student submissions in the course).

COURSES (id | course_code | name):
1 | AAA-2013J | Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)
2 | AAA-2014J | Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)
3 | BBB-2013J | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013)
4 | BBB-2014J | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)
5 | BBB-2013B | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013)
6 | BBB-2014B | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)
7 | CCC-2014J | Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)
8 | CCC-2014B | Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)
9 | DDD-2013J | Data-Driven Design (Fall 2013)
10 | DDD-2014J | Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)
11 | DDD-2013B | Data-Driven Design (Spring 2013)
12 | DDD-2014B | Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)
13 | EEE-2013J | Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2013)
14 | EEE-2014J | Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)
15 | EEE-2014B | Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)
16 | FFF-2013J | Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013)
17 | FFF-2014J | Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)
18 | FFF-2013B | Foundations of Finance (Spring 2013)
19 | FFF-2014B | Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014)
20 | GGG-2013J | Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2013)
21 | GGG-2014J | Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)
22 | GGG-2014B | Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)

HOW TO EXTRACT EACH METRIC (verified working):
- TA_Count: call mcp__canvas__canvas_get_course_grades with course_id=<id> and type=["TaEnrollment"]. The response has "pagination": {"total_count": N}. Use pagination.total_count as TA_Count. If has_more is true, page through with page=2 etc. and sum total counts (unlikely; usually 1 page). Do NOT use canvas_list_course_users (it lacks role info).
- Assignment_Count: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments with course_id=<id>. Count the number of assignment objects in the returned JSON array (all are published).
- Submission_Count: call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions with course_id=<id> and per_page=100. WARNING: the output can be huge (60KB+) and will be truncated and saved to a file at a path like /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-ta-workload-excel-email/workspace/.tool_results/mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions-<callid>.txt. Read that file (use mcp__filesystem__read_text_file on the output_path, reading the tail) to find the "pagination" object at the end: use "total_count" as Submission_Count. Do NOT count the submission objects manually. Do NOT use per-assignment summary totals (bulk total is authoritative). If the file is not available, retry the call and read the saved file.

PROCESS:
1. For each of the 22 courses, call the three tools (you may batch several courses' calls in parallel within a single message to speed things up, e.g., 4-6 courses at a time).
2. Build a list of dicts: {"course_id": id, "course_name": name, "course_code": code, "ta_count": N, "assignment_count": N, "submission_count": N}.
3. Write this raw list to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-ta-workload-excel-email/workspace/course_metrics_raw.json using mcp__filesystem__write_file (pretty-printed JSON).
4. Then compute the report dataset:
   - Submissions_Per_TA for each course = round(Submission_Count / TA_Count, 1) using round-half-up (i.e., floor(x*10 + 0.5)/10). If TA_Count == 0, Submissions_Per_TA = 0.0.
   - Sort the course rows alphabetically by Course_Name (full name as listed above, e.g., "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)").
   - Summary values: Total_Courses = 22; Total_TAs = sum of all ta_count; Avg_TAs_Per_Course = round(Total_TAs / 22, 1) (round-half-up to 1 decimal); Max_Assignment_Count = max assignment_count; Most_Loaded_Course = course name with the highest Submissions_Per_TA (tie-break: alphabetically first course name).
5. Write the final computed dataset to /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-ta-workload-excel-email/workspace/report_data.json as JSON with structure:
{
  "course_workload": [ {"Course_Name": ..., "Course_Code": ..., "TA_Count": ..., "Assignment_Count": ..., "Submission_Count": ..., "Submissions_Per_TA": ...}, ... ],  // sorted by Course_Name
  "summary": {"Total_Courses": 22, "Total_TAs": ..., "Avg_TAs_Per_Course": ..., "Max_Assignment_Count": ..., "Most_Loaded_Course": ...}
}
Use mcp__filesystem__write_file.

VERIFICATION (required before finishing):
- Verify every one of the 22 courses appears exactly once in course_metrics_raw.json and report_data.json.
- Sanity check: submission_count should be >= 0 for all; ta_count >= 0.
- Report back: the full contents of report_data.json (all course rows + summary) in your final summary, plus confirmation that both JSON files were written.

DELIVERABLE: Both JSON files written to the workspace, and your final message must contain the complete report_data.json content (every course row and the summary) so the main agent can use it without re-reading files.
